chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from al-Riḍā عليه السلام, he said:

The water of the well is ample; nothing renders it najis except if its smell or its taste changes. Then water is drawn from it until the smell goes away and its taste becomes good, because it has a source.

So the meaning in this report is that nothing spoils it in such a way that use of any part of it is impermissible unless all of it must be drawn out, except what changes it. As for that which does not change it, then a measured amount is drawn from it and use is made of the remainder, according to what we explained in the Book of Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām.

key_terms.رِيحُهُ: its smell, one of the indicators of change in the water
key_terms.طَعْمُهُ: its taste, one of the indicators of change in the water
key_terms.فَيُنْزَحُ: then water is drawn out from it
key_terms.لَا يُنَجِّسُهُ: does not render it najis or impure
key_terms.مَاءُ الْبِئْرِ: the water of a well, discussed here as a source of taharah and use
key_terms.مَادَّةً: a replenishing source or supply feeding the well
key_terms.يُغَيِّرُهُ: changes it, meaning alters one of its perceptible qualities
key_terms.يُنْتَفَعُ بِالْبَاقِي: the remainder may still be used

ai.seo_question: When does something make well water najis in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This report explains the ruling of well water in cases of contamination. Well water is not considered najis merely by something falling into it unless one of its qualities, such as smell or taste, changes; if no such change occurs, a specified amount may be drawn while the rest remains usable.
